sections.heading: SIX GUNS, SIX PEOPLE, SIX DAYS — KEEP GOING
sections.content:
Q: Six Guns, Six People, Six Days — even at a pace of one volume a year, that's fine, just please, whatever happens, get it out! Please don't let it die as an unfinished project!

A: It'd be nice if I could get one out before the year's over.[ref:sixguns-vol2]

sections.heading: AKKYUN'S DAUGHTER NEEDS A NAME
sections.content:
Q: I read the story about Akkyun's daughter! At first I was like "wait, who is this?!", but eventually I figured out what was going on. It was incredibly fun, and that unhinged feeling had me completely hooked! I'd love to know the daughter's name… └( 'ω')┘

A: Ah, now that you mention it, it never actually comes up in the story. What should I do about that.

sections.heading: MORE LIAR, BROKEN, PLEASE
sections.content:
Q: The Liar, Broken short story was wonderful. Even though things are a little twisted, seeing Akkyun and Ma-chan still alive and together was really comforting. If there's ever a chance, I'd love to see the story continue as a short-story collection, something like a "Liar, Broken i."

A: I can't think of any ideas for it, and Sa-sensei is busy too… Not that it's related, but the demo for Toukiden was pretty fun.[ref:toukiden-hidari]

sections.heading: A WISH LIST OF LIAR, BROKEN CAMEOS
sections.content:
Q: Every day I find myself looking forward to updates. Is there a sequel to Liar, Broken? Please write one. I'd love to read interactions between ××'s child and the other characters — Dr. Koibi, Geronimo, Nancy, the little sister, Kouta, Kyouko, Yuzu, Kazuki, the nurse, and if possible, Tooe too. (If you can, please write Dr. Koibi!) Now and forever, I'll keep looking forward to your work. Please keep at it! — Sincerely, One of the Rabble

A: If it ever got animated, I'd probably write ten-plus volumes, ha ha ha… well, that's obviously never happening. Apparently it's too grotesque for that.

sections.heading: WRITE US A HIGH SCHOOL FRESHMAN STORY
sections.content:
Q: Please write a novel themed around "high school freshmen"! You can mix it with other themes too. Sorry for such a shameless request.

A: Adachi and Shimamura are high school freshmen! Are there any other first-years I'm missing?[ref:adachi-freshman]

sections.heading: I LOST MY WILL TO LIVE
sections.content:
Q: Thank you for all the wonderful work you've done! Of your books, I love Liar, Broken the most — but once I finished it, I lost all purpose in living! So please, give me a sequel. Give me something to live for!

A: Hmm… honestly, I want to write something far more interesting than that one. Would that not work instead?

sections.heading: BECOME MY BRIDE
sections.content:
Q: Become my (♂) bride, Iruma!

A: (pretends not to see this)

sections.heading: ENLISTING SIGHT UNSEEN
sections.content:
Q: Iruma Hitoma-sensei! Nice to meet you! This is my very first email! I've been reading your work since my first year of high school. Your stories have really broadened my sense of values! I'll keep supporting you from here on out too! By the way, I'd also like to enlist in the Iruma Legion.

A: It's a "legion," but you say you want to "enlist"? Does that even track? What is this? Well, whatever — come on in, come on in.

sections.heading: NOT ENOUGH AKKYUN
sections.content:
Q: Sensei, I really love Akkyun. It's Love, you know. But lately there hasn't been enough Akkyun content and it's killing me. Please give me some Akkyun. orz

A: Go read the web novel! And if that's still not enough, I'm sorry.

sections.heading: A SEQUEL TO MY SMALL-SCALE MIRACLE?
sections.content:
Q: Won't you publish a sequel to My Small-Scale Miracle? I really loved Blue Shirt and his conversations with her![ref:blue-shirt]

A: I don't really have any ideas for it right now… though a short story is probably doable.

sections.heading: THE ALIEN MYSTERY IN ADACHI AND SHIMAMURA
sections.content:
Q: Hello! I read Adachi and Shimamura (´▽｀*), and I immediately came here to ask a question — I feel like this volume ended on a bit of a half-finished note. The mystery of the alien girl's fate, and how things are progressing between Adachi and Shimamura… I really hope you keep writing it. Is there a sequel planned?

A: It'll come out in September. But don't expect the alien mystery to be resolved.

sections.heading: DOES IRUMA HAVE A BEST FRIEND?
sections.content:
Q: I've always loved Iruma-sensei's work. By the way, does Iruma-sensei have a best friend? I only ever seem to form relationships that are broad but shallow. Is that okay?

A: I don't have a single one. If anything, I don't even have regular friends. That said, if you do have friends, I don't think you need to force yourself to worry about this kind of thing. I don't really understand what qualifies as a "best" friend either. If you bind your relationships to a name or a standard, I think they'll stagnate and rot.

sections.heading: PUBLISH THE 6000-YEN BOOKLET
sections.content:
Q: So, um — I have a proposal… Would it be possible to publish something like Marumaru Issatsu Iruma Hitoma as an actual book? A web release would work too. The other day I tried to get a copy, but the price was already pushing 6000 yen… I really can't afford that. Please, please consider it![ref:marumaru-booklet]

A: 6000 yen?! Maybe I should just start selling it myself… ahem. A web release is something I could consider, but the stuff collected in there is all pretty unusual writing — can that stuff even be properly published?[ref:marumaru-stories]

sections.heading: THE MAGAZINE-ONLY CROSSOVERS
sections.content:
Q: I've always loved reading Iruma-sensei's work. This is a sudden question, but there are all kinds of crossovers across your works, and I haven't managed to keep track of all of them. Part of the reason is that some were only ever published in the magazine. Will we ever get the chance to read those pieces in some other form, going forward?

A: Magazine-only pieces… are there any? We'll look into various formats, including short-story collections.

sections.heading: TWELVE HOURS A DAY
sections.content:
Q: I'd like to join the Iruma Legion. How many hours a day do you spend writing novels? What do you think of the line "to become a novelist is to give up being human"?

A: On days I'm writing, it's about twelve hours; on days I'm not, it's genuinely zero. And as for that line — hmm, well — I think that no matter how amazing a technique or a work someone creates, it's still, in the end, something made by a human being. Because I'm human — ah, I'm not joking around here.

sections.heading: A KISOGAWA SIDE STORY, PLEASE
sections.content:
Q: Hello, Iruma-sama. I love the Hanasaki Tarou series, and I especially love Kisogawa! So, would you write a side story starring Kisogawa? I'm begging you. (dogeza)

A: Well then — I'll write it sometime this year and put it up on the site, probably.

sections.heading: TWELVE VOLUMES IN TWELVE MONTHS?
sections.content:
Q: I love Liar, Broken the most, and reading your work has really shifted my values quite a bit. I hope you'll do something like Nishio Isin did — publishing one volume a month for twelve straight months.[ref:katanagatari]

A: To begin with, I'm just not the type who could write an entire twelve-volume long-form series… I'd definitely run out of ideas partway through.

sections.heading: A BISHOUJO GAME FOR ELLIO?
sections.content:
Q: Right now, as we speak, I'm working hard to raise Ellio's affection level in Yome Kore.[ref:yome-kore] Does Iruma-sensei play any gal games? I'd love it if there were a bishoujo game with Ellio in it.

A: I've played Remember11.[ref:remember11] Though there weren't many bishoujo in that one.

sections.heading: JOINING WITHOUT BECOMING A NOVELIST
sections.content:
Q: Hello, I've always loved your work. But my dream for the future isn't to become a novelist. If I end up finding a job I can support myself with someday, could I still join the Iruma Legion?

A: No problem at all, though we don't have any membership perks, you know? You won't get any ginger sauce or anything like that.

sections.heading: A MEDIEVAL EUROPEAN FANTASY?
sections.content:
Q: I'd love to read a fantasy work by Iruma-sensei set in medieval Europe. I'm very curious what would happen if the realistic worldview you write blended with fantasy elements.

A: I imagine it'd end up being a story about a bald village chief who uses magic that can only summon bones.

sections.heading: WILL THE DAUGHTER'S STORY BE PUBLISHED?
sections.content:
Q: The Lying Boy and the Broken Girl got a new start on this site.[ref:mikun-webseries] If it runs as a long-term serialization, will it eventually get a print release?

A: Sorry, that one's wrapping up this month… but I might write more short stories in that world later.

sections.heading: WRITING THE LIZARD KING WITHOUT AN OUTLINE
sections.content:
Q: It's well known that Iruma-sensei doesn't write outlines, but was even The Lizard King written without one? Honestly, being able to write something that interesting without an outline is genuinely too talented — it's disgusting, and it makes me both resentful and jealous. Let me fry up the dirt from your navel and drink it.

A: I washed my navel really thoroughly, so there's no dirt! Ah, and yes, still no outline, same as always.

sections.heading: OLDER, SAME AGE, OR YOUNGER?
sections.content:
Q: Let me ask another question, if I may. Between an older, more mature woman, a classmate, or a younger girl — if you had to date one of them, who would you choose?

A: An "older woman"… huh… Honestly, I tend to like girls younger than myself. I'm getting up there in years myself, after all.

sections.heading: WHERE ARE THE FIGURES?
sections.content:
Q: I love Liar, Broken. I bought the CD too. By the way, are figures of Yuzu and Mimouto and Akkyun still not out?! I've reached my limit!

A: You've gone past your limit — now there's someone in here I don't even recognize. Who's "Mimouto"?

sections.heading: AN ART BOOK, AND A SEASON 2?
sections.content:
Q: Ellio is super-duper cute! Will there be an art book? Also, more Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy — next volume, please! Season 2, please! I plan to buy every book Iruma-sensei ever writes, but Electric Girl is truly a god-tier work!

A: Has there really never been an art book? There's the anime version, at least… As for a Season 2 — probably not. If it happened, I'd be thrilled, though.

sections.heading: WHAT'S MAEKAWA'S FIRST NAME?
sections.content:
Q: I'll just ask straight out: what is Maekawa-san's first name? I want to call her by name so badly, oooooh!

A: Please just call her by whatever name you personally prefer.

sections.heading: DOES IRUMA LIKE CATS?
sections.content:
Q: Cats — they're so cute, right? I never get tired of petting them every single day. Does Iruma Hitoma-sensei like cats?

A: I've never lived with a cat, since saying goodbye would be too painful, but I do think they're cute to look at.

sections.heading: AN EARTH'S WORTH OF LOVE FOR AKKYUN
sections.content:
Q: I love Akkyun way too much and it's honestly painful — what should I do? Given how much I × (love) Akkyun, I could probably create an entire second Earth out of it.

A: Once you've made it, give me Manhattan Island! Ah, no, actually — Tahiti sounds better. I'm looking forward to it.

sections.heading: WHY WON'T MY FRIEND READ YOUR BOOKS?
sections.content:
Q: I'm a fan of Iruma Hitoma-sensei, but when I recommended your work to a friend, they didn't take to it. Why do you think that is?

A: Probably because there's no gravitational pull between you and that friend.

sections.heading: ANOTHER HOPEFUL RECRUIT
sections.content:
Q: I love Iruma-sensei the most! I want to become a novelist too. If it's alright, please let me join the Iruma Legion!

A: People keep joining nonstop — I wonder what number we're up to now?

sections.heading: DEBUTING OUTSIDE DENGEKI BUNKO
sections.content:
Q: If I debut through a publisher other than Dengeki Bunko, can I still join the Iruma Legion?

A: No problem at all.

sections.heading: HOW MANY YEARS UNTIL I'M YOUR BOYFRIEND?
sections.content:
Q: How many more years until I can become Iruma-sensei's boyfriend?

A: Well, how old are you, exactly?

sections.heading: FRIENDS IN THE INDUSTRY
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei have any author friends he's close with? Are there any authors you'd like to get closer to going forward? Personally, I'd love to see an interview between you and another author.

A: Forget being close — I don't even have any author acquaintances. That said, setting aside novelists specifically, there are people whose work I pay attention to, even if we're not close — Daisuke Ashihara, Hideo Kamiumi, and so on.[ref:ashihara-kamiumi]

sections.heading: A WEEKLY IRUMA HITOMA?
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-kun, your release pace has slowed down lately — what should we do about that? Please try to boost your motivation as much as possible (don't worry about sales), and aim for a "Weekly Iruma Hitoma."

A: A weekly format, huh — if there were ever a project like that, it might actually be interesting.

sections.heading: AIMING TO ANIMATE LIAR, BROKEN
sections.content:
Q: I'm currently aiming to become an animator. I want to make anime out of Iruma-sensei's work — specifically, an anime of Liar, Broken. That's the goal I get up for every day. But of course, there are times I feel discouraged. Please say "hang in there" to me.

A: Hang in there (ganbare)… what a boring line that is. Please do your best (ganbatte kudasai)!

sections.heading: THE OUT-OF-PRINT MII-KUN BOOKLET
sections.content:
Q: I've been collecting everything you've written, but no matter what I do, I can't get my hands on "Mii-kun and Ma-chan's ×× Life." Has it stopped being sold?[ref:mikun-booklet]

A: As for selling it again — that'd be a little difficult… Making the content itself available to read in some other way might be possible, though… is it possible?
Editorial note: Based on your feedback, this is currently planned to be published on Iruma no Ma at a later date.[ref:mikun-booklet-fate]

sections.heading: MORE OF ELECTRIC GIRL'S SUPPORTING CAST
sections.content:
Q: I've always loved reading your stories! I really love Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy, and while I understand it couldn't be helped, it's a shame that Ryuushi-kun and Maekawa-san barely appeared in the web-serialized sequel. I'd be happy if you could write a conversation between the two of them, or between those two and someone else.

A: Honestly, I've forgotten what those two characters were even like… ahem. To be honest, I feel like if I tried writing them again now, it'd feel off somehow — is that okay?

sections.heading: A DRAGON QUEST RECRUITMENT JOKE
sections.content:
Q: The questioner looks at Iruma as though wanting to join the Iruma Legion![ref:dq5-monster]

A: Would it be all right if I gave you a name like Tonnura?[ref:tonnura]

sections.heading: IS THE LEGION CLOSED TO NON-NOVELISTS?
sections.content:
Q: A question for Iruma-sensei! Is the Iruma Legion closed to anyone who isn't a novelist? If it's possible, I'd like to join too.

A: My gate isn't that narrow… but, um, what exactly would you be joining to do?

sections.heading: PLANNING TO JOIN NEXT YEAR
sections.content:
Q: I too am someone who wants to join the Iruma Legion. I'm planning to join the year after next!! First, I'll start by working hard on submissions… ((quietly

A: Since you've said it, make it happen! Good luck!

sections.heading: HOW MANY BOOKS WILL YOU WRITE?
sections.content:
Q: A question for Iruma-sensei — I heard that the science fiction author Isaac Asimov wrote close to four hundred books in his lifetime. How many books does Iruma-sensei plan to write in his?[ref:asimov]

A: I want to become the person who's written the most in the entire world. That's roughly the scale of thing I'm thinking about.

references.title: Six Guns, Six People, Six Days Publication Timeline
references.note: The first volume of Six Days, Six People, Six Guns was published in August 2012. Its second volume, referenced by Iruma's answer here, followed in December 2013. Its third and final volume — which brought the series to an abrupt, truncated ending — wasn't published until January 2016.

references.title: Toukiden and the Illustrator "Hidari"
references.note: Character design for Koei Tecmo's action RPG Toukiden (released July 2013 for PS Vita and PSP) was handled by the illustrator known by the pen name Hidari (左), who is also the regular cover and interior illustrator for Iruma's own Usotsuki Mii-kun to Kowareta Maa-chan (The Lying Boy and the Broken Girl) series — hence Iruma's comment about "Sa-sensei" being busy.

references.title: Freshman Protagonists in Iruma's Work
references.note: Aside from the two leads of Adachi and Shimamura, the only other freshman protagonist across Iruma Hitoma's body of work to date is Yumemi Sasaoka, lead of the 2016 magazine-serialized series Onarisan Kouryuuki.

references.title: "Blue Shirt" and My Small-Scale Miracle
references.note: "Blue Shirt" is a nickname for one of the male leads of My Small-Scale Miracle, whose real name is never given — he wears exclusively blue clothing, and it's also the pen name he uses in the crossover short story "Radio from Another Dimension." The "her" the questioner mentions is one of the story's female leads, likewise unnamed.

references.title: Marumaru Issatsu Iruma Hitoma
references.note: Properly titled Marugoto Issatsu "Iruma Hitoma," this was a promotional booklet given away with Volume 14 of Dengeki Bunko MAGAZINE in 2010, collecting several of Iruma's magazine-only short stories. Out of print, it had become a sought-after collector's item by the time of this Q&A.

references.title: The Booklet's Experimental Short Stories
references.note: The stories collected in the Marumaru Issatsu booklet include several formal experiments: "Light of the Garden" and "Garden of Light," whose paragraphs mirror each other in character count and punctuation placement; "Dog of the Road" and "Road of the Dog," which work the same way; and "Rain of the Heart," in which the text is typeset to visually resemble falling raindrops.

references.title: Daisuke Ashihara and Hideo Kamiumi
references.note: Daisuke Ashihara is a manga artist best known as the creator of World Trigger. Hideo Kamiumi is a manga artist known for SOUL CATCHER(S).

references.title: Katanagatari's Monthly Release Schedule
references.note: The questioner is referring to Nishio Isin's twelve-volume series Katanagatari, which released one volume a month, every month, from January to December 2007 — a publishing feat the questioner is asking Iruma to replicate.

references.title: Yome Kore
references.note: Yome Kore was a Japanese mobile gacha game that ran from 2011 to 2016, letting players collect a large cast of characters crossed over from various anime and games, including Fujiwa and Ellio from Iruma's Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy.

references.title: Remember11
references.note: Remember11 -the age of infinity- is a visual novel developed by KID, part of the Infinity series, known more for its puzzle-box mystery plot than for its romance elements — hence Iruma's joke that it's fairly light on bishoujo-game content.

references.title: The Web Serialization of Akkyun and Ma-chan's Daughter's Story
references.note: The questioner is referring to the web serialization "Usotsuki Mii-kun to Kowareta Maa-chan -A? New? Translation?-," which follows the daughter of the original series' two leads, Akkyun and Ma-chan.

references.title: "Mii-kun and Ma-chan's ×× Life."
references.note: This booklet was released on January 22, 2011, to commemorate the live-action film adaptation of The Lying Boy and the Broken Girl. It collected two pieces: "The Lying Mii-kun and the Broken Ma-chan: Where Fantasy Lives, Reality" and "My and Ma-chan's Diary."

references.title: The Booklet's Promised Republication
references.note: Despite the editorial note appended to this answer promising a future web release on Iruma no Ma, the content was never actually made public there.

references.title: The Dragon Quest V Monster-Recruitment Line
references.note: The questioner's framing ("looks at Iruma as though wanting to join...") mimics the on-screen prompt Dragon Quest V uses when a defeated monster asks to join the player's party.

references.title: Tonnura
references.note: Tonnura (トンヌラ) is a recurring name used, in various forms, across multiple entries in the Dragon Quest series — often for a background or joke character. Iruma is riffing on the Dragon Quest monster-naming joke from the question above.

references.title: Isaac Asimov's Prolific Output
references.note: Isaac Asimov, the American science fiction and popular-science author, is commonly cited as having written or edited close to 500 books over his career (estimates commonly range from roughly 400 to 500 depending on how the count is made), a figure the questioner rounds down to "close to four hundred."
